annotation.summary_en: In a pitch-black prison cell, a prisoner repeatedly strikes matches to wake up his cellmate, Vakho, just to ask for the time, only to be reminded that they are both serving life sentences.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch takes place in a pitch-dark room where the only source of light comes from matches being struck. A man lies in the dark and periodically strikes a match, illuminating his own face and a wind-up alarm clock sitting on a wooden table. Each time he lights a match, he wakes his cellmate, Vakho, with overly affectionate and poetic praise, calling him 'king,' 'prince,' and 'long-time friend,' just to ask for the current time. Vakho patiently answers—three o'clock, four o'clock, half-past four—while the man thanks him profusely. After several repetitions of this cycle, Vakho finally snaps, pointing out the absurdity of the situation: it doesn't matter what time it is because they have both been sentenced to life imprisonment. The darkness of the scene is finally broken by a washed-out wide shot revealing a bleak, cell-like room with a grilled window. The sketch ends with a guard or cellmate shouting for everyone to wake up because it is six o'clock, ending the repetitive cycle of the long night.
catchphrases: Վաղո ջան մի հատ ժամը չէիր ասի
Վաղո ախպեր, թագավոր ախպեր, իմ արքայազն ախպեր
